why: Both moved the identical five-call surface through one client wrap with equivalent care, but B shipped more of the judgment as working, tested code (four branches with 22 new tests versus three branches and no tests) and found things A never saw: the chart tool's Node subprocess as a fourth LLM surface, the dead [llm.<agent>] config that made per-agent routing impossible, and the enumerated defects in the 334-line Bedrock shim. On the system-level bar B also reaches further into Router — a measured Switchyard comparison (29x cheaper on a real step shape, with an honest n=4 caveat), a cheap-model-with-escalation rework built on the loop's existing is_stuck detector, and fallbacks plus provider_timeout scoped to the agent-step label — where A's deeper items (model choice, fallbacks, retry hygiene) all stay as prose.
A_best: The narrowest defensible unlock: naming api.anthropic.com alone and explaining exactly why Ollama, Jiekou, PPIO and Google were left out, with a trace-verified check that the shipped claude-3-7-sonnet pin correctly stays on the provider — the migration half is honest, reversible and cleanly evidenced.
B_best: i3 — noticing that BaseAgent.llm defaults to LLM(), so the validator's per-agent branch never ran and [llm.manus]/[llm.browser] were advertised-but-dead config, then fixing it and making it the hinge for per-agent models, cache keys, tiers and timeouts. That is a product-level finding, not a migration finding.
A_worst: Too much of the real judgment is deferred: model choice, fallbacks, retry hygiene, reasoning-effort and usage accounting are all unbuilt prose, no new tests were written, and i1's claim that the cache key is 'a no-op on Claude because the runtime already sets it' is contradicted by B's direct measurement that nothing cached without the key.
B_worst: The per-agent-llm branch fails the outside check's parse gate with a SyntaxError in data_visualization.py, so the single best item is not shippable as committed; and unlocking whatever host config.toml names can silently divert reseller traffic (PPIO, Jiekou) to Router's own provider for colliding open-weight ids — disclosed, but a broader blast radius than A's one named host.
